question: Should Twilio RCS become a bundled OpenClaw channel, or should it ship as an external ClawHub/plugin package with only the necessary generic SDK safety seam upstreamed?
rationale: Both shapes are technically plausible, but bundling commits core to a large provider-backed configuration, webhook, documentation, and support surface; repository policy and the paired feature issue leave that ownership choice to maintainers.

options.title: External plugin plus SDK seam
options.body: Keep RCS independently installable and upstream only the generic route-registration ownership signal needed for safe SMS coexistence.

options.title: Sponsor bundled RCS
options.body: Accept RCS as a core-distributed channel after live proof, receipt persistence, dependency authorization, upgrade documentation, and focused compatibility validation are complete.

options.title: Pause pending adoption evidence
options.body: Leave the feature issue and PR open without landing until live deployments demonstrate enough demand and operational stability to choose permanent ownership.

recommendation.title: External plugin plus SDK seam
recommendation.body: Keep RCS independently installable and upstream only the generic route-registration ownership signal needed for safe SMS coexistence.

likelyOwner.reason: The bundled Twilio SMS channel is the closest product precedent, and its introducer is the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether RCS belongs at the same distribution tier.
